rounds.response: Most likely cause: a benign heater closed‑loop transient (thermal lag from prior extended payload ops) — supported by the simultaneous short heater current step and small, self‑recovering ~0.3–0.4 V bus dip with no limit trips; no evidence in the supplied packets of latch‑up or permanent EPS fault (speculative, based on the reduced summary). Risk to the ~3‑hr trim burn is low if telemetry remains stable because bus and Battery B returned to expected curves. Recommend targeted pre‑burn checks: confirm battery SOC/temperatures and that Battery B discharge trend has fully rejoined predictions, verify MPPT/array and EPS regulator status, and inspect heater controller mode/setpoints for any unintended changes. Operationally, increase EPS/power telemetry cadence through eclipse exit and the burn window and adopt a simple go/no‑go rule to hold the burn if the bus dips >0.5 V or battery discharge remains >~15% above predicted at burn time. If no recurrence, proceed as planned with heightened monitoring; if it repeats, delay the burn and run EPS diagnostics.
